testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air, what does this mean?

options.text: This is normal and you should not worry.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air to prevent pressure from getting too high. If air is being released, something is wrong. Have a mechanic repair the problem.

questions.question: What happens if your engine does not have enough oil?

options.text: The vehicle will have trouble stopping.
The vehicle will jerk while you drive.
The engine can be damaged very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be damaged very quickly.
questions.explanation: Your engine needs enough oil to run properly. Without oil, an engine can be destroyed very fast.

questions.question: A smaller vehicle than yours will usually:

options.text: Take longer to stop than your vehicle.
Take about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can usually stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far to stay behind other vehicles.

questions.question: What tread depth is required in every major groove of a front tire?
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread in every major groove on front tires. Other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should move no more than:
questions.explanation: Park on level ground and set wheel chocks. Pull the slack adjusters to check they do not move more than one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: In a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than ____ psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle should lose no more than 5 psi of air pressure in one minute. If it loses air faster than this, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, you should NOT:

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services with your location.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.question: When are you most likely to encounter strong winds?
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. You are especially likely to encounter strong winds when coming out of a tunnel.

questions.question: Who is responsible for cargo loaded onto a truck?

options.text: The person who loaded the cargo

questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for cargo, even if they did not load it. You must inspect the cargo and make sure it is secured properly.

questions.question: When should you inspect cargo during a trip?

options.text: Only have another driver inspect it.
Only after the trip is finished.
Every time you take a break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you take a break.
questions.explanation: Inspect your cargo and how it is secured every time you take a break. Check it at least every 150 miles.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is usually:
questions.explanation: Hanging meat can be unstable. The meat swings during transport and has a high center of gravity.

questions.question: If you cannot tell if the road is icy and slippery, what should you do?

options.text: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think ice may be forming, open your window and touch the front of the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice is on these items, the road is likely becoming icy.

questions.question: A 10-foot load must be secured with at least:
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo must have at least two tie-downs, regardless of size.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, what must you do?

options.text: The State will inform your employer.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction. You must also inform your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. Parking tickets do not apply to this rule.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one air system is very low on pressure, what happens?

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one air system loses pressure. If air pressure gets too low while driving, you should exit the road and park as soon as possible.

questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:
questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile phone while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice on road surfaces is called:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks wet. Be careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: Wheel rims that have been welded should:

options.text: Be placed on the rear tires.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe and should not be used.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals and check your mirrors when changing lanes.

questions.question: When alley docking, what should you do first?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: First, pull past the alley and stop parallel to its outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking area. Park in a straight line within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When parking in an offset back/left space, what should you do?

options.text: Go straight forward, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then go forward to the left.
Go straight forward, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight forward, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, go straight forward first, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must be completely inside the parking space lines.

questions.question: When checking your mirrors, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the passenger side mirror.
Do not use the driver's side mirror.
Use mirrors on both sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use mirrors on both sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Check both side mirrors while driving. You need to know what is behind and beside your vehicle at all times.

questions.question: What can affect how far your vehicle travels before stopping?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your vehicle's speed, weight, and how much grip the road gives your tires.

questions.question: How should cargo in a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no more than three feet high.
It should be secured so it does not move.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured so it does not move.
questions.explanation: Cargo in a trailer must be secured to prevent it from shifting during transport.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which belt do you NOT need to check?
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: How should you drive a large truck to avoid slowing down traffic?

options.text: Pass other vehicles while going uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your truck cannot keep up with other traffic, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Why should you accelerate slowly on a slippery surface?

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
To keep control of your vehicle.
So you do not go faster than the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep control of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly in poor conditions like rain or snow to avoid losing control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget to check something.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget to check something.
questions.explanation: Use the same inspection steps every time. This helps you remember all the important items to check.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, complete a full inspection and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: What does alcohol usually do to driving ability?

options.text: It makes it harder to judge distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It makes it harder to judge distance.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts many skills needed for safe driving, including coordination, reaction time, depth perception, and night vision. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required safety equipment?
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or three liquid burning flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 3 psi in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: Over-length loads require:

options.text: Roads to be closed to other traffic
A person to walk alongside the vehicle

questions.explanation: Over-length, over-width, and overweight loads need special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: Where must placards be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo?

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle
On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle
Only on the driver's side of the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle
questions.explanation: Placards must be on the front, rear, and both sides of a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo so they can be seen from any direction.

questions.question: Unsafely reaching for a phone while driving is:

options.text: Acceptable if you are driving without a passenger
Acceptable if you plan to use a hands-free feature
Never acceptable, even if you plan to use a hands-free feature

questions.correctAnswerText: Never acceptable, even if you plan to use a hands-free feature
questions.explanation: Your phone must be within easy reach while you stay securely in your seat. Reaching unsafely for a phone is dangerous and not allowed, even if you will use a hands-free feature.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, where should your vehicle be at the end of each exercise?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described
In the exact position the examiner described
Within three feet of the position the examiner described

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. Not doing so can cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: How should a truck be parked?

options.text: So it must be backed up to leave the space
So it can be pulled forward to leave the space

questions.correctAnswerText: So it can be pulled forward to leave the space
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Always park in spaces where you can drive forward to leave.

questions.question: What is a danger of swerving to avoid a hazard in a large truck?

options.text: The truck may miss the object
The truck may stay in the same lane

questions.explanation: Top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers may flip over when swerving.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You get an extra point against your final score
You automatically fail the entire test

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire test
questions.explanation: You must face the vehicle and use three points of contact when exiting. For buses, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly results in automatic failure.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. This gives you more room to stop smoothly and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass.

questions.question: Why should you drain the air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil. These build up in the air storage tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks to remove these buildups. On tanks with a manual drain valve, drain them at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: When changing lanes, but only when other vehicles are nearby.
When changing lanes, but only if it is dark outside.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors for traffic before changing lanes. Check mirrors often as part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: ____ are most affected by strong winds.
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it harder for a driver to control their vehicle. This is especially true for drivers of lighter vehicles.

questions.question: What are alcohol evaporators?

options.text: Devices that add alcohol to air brake systems.
Only allowed in the northern parts of the state.

questions.correctAnswerText: Devices that add alcohol to air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have alcohol evaporators. These devices add alcohol to the braking system to prevent ice from forming.

questions.question: What does an alcohol evaporator do in an air brake system?

options.text: Makes the brakes work without squeaking.
Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
Lubricates parts of the braking system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an evaporator that adds alcohol to the system. The alcohol helps prevent ice from forming inside the system.

questions.question: If you are unsure how to put out a vehicle fire, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you do not know which fire extinguisher to use, especially for a hazardous materials fire, wait for firefighters to arrive. Let them put out the fire safely.

questions.question: Which item is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake system parts include: air compressor, compressor governor, air storage tanks, tank drains, alcohol evaporator, safety valve, brake pedal, foundation brakes, pressure gauges, low air pressure warning signal, stop light switch, front brake limiting valve, spring brakes, and parking brake controls.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on roads with less traction. On a wet road, reduce your speed by about one-third.

questions.question: If you must back up using driver's side backing, this practice:

options.text: Is only recommended if it is raining.

questions.explanation: If you must back up, back toward the driver's side of the vehicle. As the driver, you will have the best view of where you are going.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) vehicles have ____ warning lamps to show when ABS is not working.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow warning lamps. They alert you when the braking system is not working. Know where your vehicle's warning lamp is before you drive.
